key_insight: The paper makes RUDE-based constitutive models more stable, thermodynamically admissible, and interpretable by combining logarithmic input compression, a split-network architecture, and a differentiable projection onto the Clausius--Duhem constraint.
engineering_relevance: These improvements make data-driven rheology more reliable for CFD and polymer-processing simulations, especially for materials with broad relaxation spectra and strong nonlinear response.
method: Log-compress input invariants to improve conditioning during training.
Use a split-network mmRUDE architecture to better organize multi-mode corrections.
Apply a differentiable projection layer to enforce thermodynamic admissibility at every time step.
evidence_signal: The models were trained on LAOS data for both a synthetic multi-mode Giesekus system and an entangled silicone polymer melt, and they remained accurate and stable on unseen shear, stress-growth, and extensional flows.
watch_item: The framework still depends on quality training data and careful implementation of the projection and tensor-basis network, which may add complexity in deployment.
paper_title: Stable and Interpretable Multi-Mode Rheological Universal Differential Equations (mmRUDEs) for Data-Driven Constitutive Modeling
